title: E7 evidence-chain checkpoint form B
instructions: Develop a body paragraph from these original practice notes: At a community seed exchange, visitors repeatedly placed seed packets on the wrong tables. Mira trialled large labels showing plant type and sowing month, then watched which questions visitors still asked. Use only the stated evidence.

parts.prompt: Which paragraph promise can be developed most convincingly from the notes?

options.text: Clear labels helped visitors sort most packets independently while revealing what guidance was still missing.
Gardening is the best hobby for every person.
Community events should always use colourful decorations.
Mira created a perfect system that could never fail.

choice_rationales.A: This bounded claim includes both the observed benefit and the remaining questions.
choice_rationales.B: The notes concern sorting guidance, not the universal value of gardening.
choice_rationales.C: Decoration is not the tested method.
choice_rationales.D: The remaining questions directly contradict a claim of perfection.

parts.hint: Protected checkpoint: no hint is available.
parts.correct_explanation: The strongest promise is precise enough to prove and honest enough to include the trial's limit.

parts.prompt: Which detail most directly demonstrates the method rather than merely describing the setting?

options.text: The exchange took place in a room with folding chairs.
Each table label paired a plant category with the month in which its seeds were normally sown.
The building had a tiled entrance.

choice_rationales.A: Furniture does not explain how the sorting method worked.
choice_rationales.B: This specifies the information structure visitors used to classify packets.
choice_rationales.C: The bags do not influence the trial's reasoning.
choice_rationales.D: The entrance material is unrelated to packet placement.

parts.hint: Protected checkpoint: no hint is available.
parts.correct_explanation: The paired category-and-month label is the observable procedure that the paragraph needs to evaluate.

parts.prompt: Which consequence-and-significance sentence best develops the observation that visitors still asked about packets with unfamiliar local names?

options.text: This showed that the broad labels reduced routine uncertainty but needed examples of local names before they could guide every visitor.
This proved that labels never work.
The questions were questions, and people often ask them.
Exactly 88.6 per cent of all confusion disappeared, although no count was made.

choice_rationales.A: This interprets both the value and the specific limit of the trial.
choice_rationales.B: Remaining uncertainty does not erase the method's stated benefit.
choice_rationales.C: The circular statement does not explain what the observation means.

parts.hint: Protected checkpoint: no hint is available.
parts.correct_explanation: Good development uses the exception to refine the claim rather than to overstate success or failure.
